title: All-hands engagement experimentation plan and executive update script
summary: Proposal and runbook for a 3-phase all-hands experimentation series focused on increasing staff participation and cross-team signal capture. Includes OKR alignment, exec update script, run-of-show, measurement plan, risk mitigation, and immediate action items.
body: Context: Our company all-hands has steady attendance but declining active participation (questions, demo submissions, pulse feedback). Leadership wants a brief, low-friction set of experiments to: 1) increase live participation by at least 25% vs baseline; 2) surface 10 high-quality cross-team signals (risks/opportunities) per event; 3) shorten broadcast time to 60 minutes while improving perceived usefulness in the post-event survey. This doc outlines a three-phase plan (pilot, iterate, scale), the proposed OKR mapping, an "exec update" script for the CEO + exec leads, the run-of-show variants, measurement approach, and a rehearsal checklist.
objectives_and_key_results: O1: Improve all-hands engagement and signal capture across the company this quarter
KR1.1: Live participation (questions + chat threads) up 25% from March baseline
KR1.2: Minimum 10 unique cross-team issues surfaced and ticketed per all-hands
O2: Tighten exec updates to be outcome-focused and demo-lite
KR2.1: Executive update blocks average <= 6 minutes each
KR2.2: 95% of exec updates include one measurable outcome or ask
three_phase_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot week, 1 event): Run two micro-experiments in parallel (’pod breakout’ and ’live lightning demos’). Keep the audience to company all-hands size but recruit 6 volunteer pod facilitators.
Phase 2 (Iterate, next 2 events): Incorporate feedback, drop the lower-performing format, tighten run-of-show, and add a 10-minute anonymous hot-issue capture moment with tagging for owners.
Phase 3 (Scale, remaining quarter): Standardize the best format, update the all-hands page template, and integrate automated tickets for captured issues into the company backlog pipeline.
run_of_show_pod_format: (60 minutes total) 0:00–05:00 — Welcome & one-sentence CEO context; 05:00–20:00 — 3 x exec outcome updates (5 minutes each + 1 clarifying Q), 20:00–35:00 — Pod breakout (10 pods, 6 people each, 8 minutes discussion, 2 minute note capture), 35:00–45:00 — Lightning highlights from pods (5 pods selected, 2 minutes each), 45:00–55:00 — Live lightning demos (3 demos, 3 minutes each), 55:00–60:00 — Close, immediate asks, pulse link and ticketing reminder.
run_of_show_lightning_only: (45 minutes total) 0:00–04:00 — Quick CEO framing; 04:00–18:00 — Exec updates (4 x 3 minutes + 1 min show of a single metric), 18:00–35:00 — 6x 2.5-minute lightning demos; 35:00–42:00 — Open floor rapid Q (moderated); 42:00–45:00 — Close & 24h follow-up actions posted.
exec_update_script: Script framework for execs: 1) headline (one sentence, outcome), 2) 1 metric that changed since the last all-hands and what we did, 3) 1 concrete ask of the company or a micro-decision requested, 4) optional 15–30 second demo link in shared deck. Example: 'Headline: Delighting ML customers with latency improvements. Metric: 99th percentile token latency down 18% since last all-hands after batching and kernel swap (see runbook PR #432). Ask: Volunteer cross-functional testers for the next 2-week canary — signup in the pulse sheet.' Keep to 6 minutes total.
measurement_plan: Baseline metrics (last 3 all-hands): unique live questioners, chat thread posts, demo submissions, post-event survey response rate and NPS. Key event metrics to track: live active participants, number of tickets auto-created from 'hot-issue capture', demo feedback score, time-per-block adherence, and survey NPS. Data owners: Analytics (Diego) will produce a 48-hour summary report; CommOps (Maya) will post takeaways and action list within 24h. Success definition for pilot: Move at least two KRs and produce a feasible roll plan.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Pods feel like mandatory extra work — emphasize voluntary signups and micro-roles (scribe, speaker, timekeeper). Risk: Execs overrun their time — enforce a visible timer and pre-event rehearsal + cold email reminder. Risk: Poor post-event pulse — automate reminders and make the pulse a 90-second single-sentence format to increase response rate.
communication_samples: Announcement email subject: 'Experimenting with a shorter, higher-engagement all-hands — signups open' Body: Hi all — This quarter we're piloting a new all-hands format designed to surface cross-team signals and reduce length to ~60 minutes. If you'd like to join as a pod facilitator or demo slot, sign up here: <signup link>. We'll publish the follow-up action list within 24 hours. — Priya
Pulse question sample: 'In one sentence, what was the most useful part of today? (optional: paste a link to a doc or ticket)'
rehearsal_checklist: Book dry-run with CEO + 3 execs 48 hours before event
Confirm pod facilitators and share facilitation notes
Enable breakout rooms and test auto-ticketing flow with Analytics
Load slide deck to company repo and lock edits 24 hours prior
Assign timer host and Slack monitoring owner
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Approve pilot (Priya) — run both pod and lightning experiments in March all-hands
2025-02-21: Ask: Shortlist demo submissions to 12 and pre-record acceptance clips (Maya)
2025-02-28: Integrate auto-ticketing into the pulse form (Engineering backlog JIRA-5123)
action_items: Priya: finalize signup form and pod facilitation guide by 2025-02-18
Maya: create announcement and schedule rehearsal with execs by 2025-02-20
Diego: wire auto-ticketing prototype and test with test-event by 2025-02-25
Liam: prepare a 1-page exec update cheat sheet for all execs by 2025-02-19
notes_to_self: Keep the pilot small and time-boxed. Push for quantification in exec updates (one metric + one ask). After the pilot, run a 30-minute postmortem with helpers and capture a short FAQ for future facilitators.
next_steps: 1) Send announcement & open signups (target send: 2025-02-17), 2) Run dry-run and capture timestamps to inform the analytics pipeline, 3) Execute the pilot at the March all-hands and publish a 48-hour summary with tickets and owners.
